categoryIntro.branding: Branding work from MAZE Studio in Tashkent — from naming and visual identity to brand strategy and rollout. Every case below started with research, a positioning workshop and a clear set of business goals, then moved through identity, guidelines and the launch assets the client needed to ship the brand into the world. Most engagements take 6 to 10 weeks; a few stretch into multi-quarter rollouts. Browse the case studies for context on the brief, the process and the result, or jump to the contact form to scope your own project.
categoryIntro.rebranding: Rebranding case studies — full repositioning, identity refreshes and rollouts for established companies in Uzbekistan and Central Asia. Each project starts with a brand audit and a sharp diagnosis of why the current brand is leaving value on the table, then moves into a new strategic platform, refreshed identity system, guidelines, and the launch kit needed to take the new brand live across product, packaging, retail and digital. We work both on focused refreshes and full reinvention.
categoryIntro.identity: Visual identity systems — logos, marks, typography, color and the rules that hold them together. Identity is more than a logo: it's a system that scales from a 32-pixel favicon to a stadium banner without losing the brand's voice. Each project below shows the wordmark and supporting elements, applied in real contexts so you can judge how the system holds up under pressure. Identity engagements typically run 6 to 9 weeks.
categoryIntro.naming: Brand naming projects — strong, defensible names with trademark pre-screening, rationale and example tone-of-voice copy. Naming is the highest-leverage decision a young company makes: the wrong name costs years of marketing. We run naming as a focused 3–5 week sprint, exploring 50+ candidates per round, narrowing to a shortlist that has passed trademark and domain checks, and finishing with a clear recommendation backed by strategy and example copy.
categoryIntro.packaging: Packaging design — structure, dieline, typography and finish for food, FMCG, beauty and premium goods. Packaging is where a brand meets the customer at the highest-intent moment. Every project below considered shelf context, photography on the print, regulatory copy, language localisation for Uzbek / Russian / English markets, and the finish — foil, emboss, varnish — that matches the price point. We deliver print-ready files and supervise the first production run.
categoryIntro.ui-ux: Digital product design — UI, UX, design systems and front-end-ready specs for web and mobile. Every digital case below starts with user research and a problem definition, then moves through information architecture, wireframes, hi-fi design and a component library handed off to engineering in Figma. We work with founders on 0→1 launches and with established teams on scaling design systems across product lines.
categoryIntro.print: Print design — books, reports, posters, signage and large-format. Print is unforgiving: there's no undo. Every project below was prepared with the printer in mind — paper choice, ink coverage, bleed, color profile and finish — and proofed on press where the budget allowed. We design for permanence, not screens.
categoryIntro.motion: Motion and animation — brand idents, explainer films, social cuts and product animations. Motion turns a static brand into a memorable one. Every motion project starts in After Effects or Cinema 4D from the same identity system we built, so the moving brand feels consistent with the static one. Output ranges from 5-second logo idents to 90-second explainer films.
categoryIntro.strategy: Brand strategy — positioning, brand architecture, naming systems and rollout plans. Strategy is the part of the work no one sees but everyone feels. Every strategic engagement below started with stakeholder interviews and category research, produced a positioning document and a measurable success framework, and led the visual identity that followed. Strategy alone runs 4 to 8 weeks; bundled with identity it adds 2 weeks at the front of the project.

aboutPage.metaDesc: MAZE Studio is a branding and design studio in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Since 2019 we build visual identities, logo systems and brand strategy across Central Asia.
aboutPage.heroHeading: We navigate brands through complexity to clarity.
aboutPage.heroSub: MAZE is a branding and design studio based in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Since 2019, we've built bold visual identities for startups, enterprises, and cultural institutions across Central Asia and beyond.
aboutPage.story1: MAZE was founded in Tashkent in 2019 with a simple conviction: that Central Asian brands deserve world-class design. At the time, the region's design landscape was largely derivative — copying Western trends without strategic intent.
aboutPage.story2: We built MAZE to be different. From day one, we insisted on strategy before aesthetics, on understanding a business deeply before picking up a pen. This approach won us early trust from Uzbekistan's most ambitious companies.
aboutPage.story3: Today, our work reaches millions of people daily — on product labels, apps, storefronts, and city billboards. We remain a tight-knit studio by choice: small enough to care deeply, experienced enough to deliver at scale.

faqItems.q: What's included in a brand identity package?

Yes. If the project involves confidential information, we'll sign an NDA before work begins.

branding.metaDescription: We work out what sets you apart, find a name if you need one, and design the logo, the identity and everything you launch with.
branding.title: Branding
branding.tagline: The whole brand, from the idea to the shop sign.
branding.intro: A brand is how people recognise and remember you: the name, the logo, the colours, the way you talk to customers. We start with a conversation about the business: who your customers are, what makes you different from the place next door, where you want to grow. From that comes a clear idea for the brand, a name if you need one, a logo, an identity, and everything the brand meets people with — from business cards and signage to packaging and social media.

approach.title: Getting to know you
approach.body: We talk about the business: who your customers are, what sets you apart, what you like and dislike about how you look today.

approach.title: The idea
approach.body: We put into words what the brand stands on: who it is for and what it promises. Plainly, so the whole team understands it.

approach.title: Design
approach.body: A name if needed, then the logo, colours, typefaces, photography and graphics. We show it all on a sign, a package and a social post, not on a blank page.

approach.title: Launch
approach.body: We put the rules into a brand book and prepare what you need to launch: business cards, social templates, signage, packaging.

deliverables: The brand idea: who it is for and what sets it apart
A name, if you need one
Logo and its versions for different uses
Brand colours, typefaces and graphics
A brand book on how to use it all
Everything for launch: business cards, social media, signage, packaging
branding.timeline: It depends on scope: a logo alone is quicker than a brand with a name, an identity and packaging. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins. If you have an opening or launch date, tell us at the start and we will plan around it.
branding.pricing: It depends on what's included: a logo alone, a full identity, or a whole brand with the idea, the name and packaging. Tell us about the task and your budget, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: Do we need full branding, or is a logo enough?
faq.a: If you're just starting out on a small budget, you can begin with a logo and core colours and add the rest later. If the business is growing — new locations, new products — it's worth doing the whole brand, so everything looks like one company.

faq.q: Can we keep our logo?
faq.a: Yes, if it works: people recognise it and it holds up both small and large. Then we build the identity around it. If the logo is holding you back, we'll say so plainly and suggest options.

faq.q: What's the difference between branding and rebranding?
faq.a: Branding is creating a brand from scratch. Rebranding is when you already have one, but it has aged or no longer fits the business. Not sure which you need? Tell us about the situation and we'll help.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: Time to talk: about the business, your customers, competitors and plans. If you have older materials — a logo, photos, a sign — show us; it helps.

rebranding.metaDescription: We find what in your brand works and what holds it back, refresh the logo and identity, and help you switch over smoothly.
rebranding.title: Rebranding
rebranding.tagline: Refresh the brand without losing the people who already know you.
rebranding.intro: A rebrand makes sense when the business has grown and the brand hasn't: the customers have changed, there are new products or cities, the logo looks dated. What matters most is not throwing away what people already know you for. First we look at what in the brand works and what gets in the way. Sometimes refreshing the logo and identity is enough; sometimes the brand needs rebuilding. Either way, we help plan the switch so customers recognise you in the new look.

approach.title: Review
approach.body: We look at the brand through the eyes of customers and competitors: what people recognise, what confuses them, what looks dated.

approach.title: Decision
approach.body: Together we decide what to keep and what to change: just the look, or also how you talk about yourselves.

approach.title: New identity
approach.body: We update the logo, colours, typefaces and materials, keeping what works — often the name, a colour or the mark.

approach.title: Switch-over
approach.body: We plan what changes first, what follows, and how to tell customers about the new look.

deliverables: A review of the brand: what to keep, what to change
A refreshed logo, or a new one
Colours, typefaces and graphics
A brand book with the rules
A switch-over plan: what changes, and in what order
New materials: signage, packaging, website, social media
rebranding.timeline: It depends on depth: refreshing a logo and identity is quicker than rebuilding the whole brand. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins. If the change is tied to a date, tell us at the start and we will plan around it.
rebranding.pricing: It depends on depth: refreshing a logo and identity is one job, rebuilding the brand is another. Tell us what you want to change and what your budget is, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: Won't we lose customers who have known us for years?
faq.a: You shouldn't, if the change is made with care. We keep what people recognise you by — the name, a colour, the mark — and plan in advance how to tell customers about the change.

faq.q: Do we have to change the name?
faq.a: No. Most rebrands keep the name. It's worth changing only for a serious reason: say, people mix you up with another company, or you're moving into new markets.

faq.q: What about our old business cards, signs and packaging?
faq.a: You don't have to replace everything at once. We start with what's most visible — signage, the website, packaging — and replace the rest as old stock runs out.

faq.q: How do we know it is time to rebrand?
faq.a: It usually shows in small things: you're embarrassed to hand over a business card, customers mix you up with competitors, the brand doesn't fit your new products or prices. If that sounds familiar, tell us about it and we'll take a look.

identity.metaDescription: Logo, colours, typefaces and a brand book, so your business is recognised the same way on a business card, a sign, a website and social media.
identity.title: Visual Identity
identity.tagline: So people recognise you everywhere, from a business card to a shop sign.
identity.intro: A visual identity is the set of rules people recognise you by: the logo, colours, typefaces, photography and graphics. With one in place, every flyer, post or sign looks like part of the same company, even when different people make them. We design identities that are easy to use day to day: clear rules, ready files and examples on your real materials.

approach.title: Getting to know you
approach.body: We learn what the business does, who your customers are and where they see you. If you already have an identity, we look at what in it works.

approach.title: Directions
approach.body: We show a few distinct directions, already on a business card, a sign and social media, so you can see how each would live.

approach.title: Refinement
approach.body: We choose a direction together and finish it: logo, colours, typefaces, graphics.

approach.title: Brand book
approach.body: We put the rules into a brand book and hand over files that are easy for you, other designers and printers to work with.

deliverables: Logo and its versions for different uses
Brand colours and typefaces
Graphics, icons or patterns, if needed
Guidance for photos and images
A brand book on how to use the identity
Examples on materials: business card, letterhead, social media, signage
Files for print and for screen
identity.timeline: It depends on scope: a logo with the core materials is quicker than a full brand book. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins.
identity.pricing: It depends on scope: a logo with the core materials, or a full brand book covering many uses. Tell us about the task and your budget, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: Can we order just a logo?
faq.a: Yes. But a logo alone is usually not enough: for everything to look consistent you also need colours and typefaces. We'll suggest the minimum that makes sense for you.

faq.q: What's the difference between an identity and a brand book?
faq.a: The identity is the logo, colours and typefaces themselves. The brand book is the manual: how and where to use them so nothing breaks.

faq.q: Will the identity work on social media and on packaging?
faq.a: Yes. Before anything is approved, we test it on different materials: at small sizes, on dark backgrounds, in print and on screen.

faq.q: We already have a logo. Can you build the identity around it?
faq.a: Yes, if the logo works. If it's holding you back, we'll say so and suggest what to do with it.

naming.metaDescription: Names for companies and products that are easy to say and remember in Uzbek, Russian and English.
naming.title: Naming
naming.tagline: A name that's easy to say, remember and find.
naming.intro: A good name is easy to say, easy to remember and easy to find online, and it doesn't sound odd in any language your customers speak. We start with what the name should convey and who it is for. Then we come up with options, check how they sound and what they mean in Uzbek, Russian and English, and see whether the domains are free and whether other companies use similar names. You choose from a shortlist of names you can actually take to market.

approach.title: The task
approach.body: We work out what exactly we're naming, who it is for and which languages the name has to work in.

approach.title: Options
approach.body: We come up with many options in different directions, from plain descriptive names to invented words.

approach.title: Checks
approach.body: We drop names that sound wrong, get confused with other companies or sound unfortunate in one of the languages. We check which domains are free.

approach.title: Choice
approach.body: We present a shortlist, explain each name and show how it looks on a sign and in an ad.

deliverables: A shortlist of strong names
Why each one fits
Sound and meaning checked in Uzbek, Russian and English
Free domains checked
A search for similar names used by other companies
Examples: the name on a sign and in an ad
naming.timeline: It depends on the task: naming one product is quicker than naming a company that is entering several markets. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins.
naming.pricing: It depends on the task: a name for one product or for a company, and in how many languages and markets it has to work. Tell us about the project and your budget, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: Do you register the trademark?
faq.a: We don't register it ourselves: a lawyer or patent attorney does that. We check in advance for very similar names to lower the risk of a refusal, but only the official examination gives the final answer.

faq.q: Will the name sound right in Uzbek, Russian and English?
faq.a: That's one of the main checks. We look at how the name is pronounced and what it means in each language, so there are no awkward associations.

faq.q: Can you design the logo too?
faq.a: Yes. A name and an identity work well done together: the designers know the name and why it was chosen from the start.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: Tell us what we're naming and for whom, what your competitors are called and what definitely won't work. If you have ideas of your own, share them; that helps too.

packaging.metaDescription: Packaging and label design for food, cosmetics and other products: packaging that gets noticed on the shelf and goes to print without trouble.
packaging.title: Packaging
packaging.tagline: So your product gets picked up off the shelf.
packaging.intro: A shopper decides in a few seconds whether to pick a product up or walk past. Packaging has to say at once what it is, who it's for and why it's worth trying. We look at the shelf the way a shopper does: what sits next to you, how to stand out, what must be on the pack. We design labels, boxes and bags for a single product or a whole range, with text in the languages you need and files your printer will accept without trouble.

approach.title: The shelf
approach.body: We look at where the product will stand and what's around it: competitors, prices, how products in the category usually look.

approach.title: The idea
approach.body: We decide what the pack should tell the shopper first, and offer design directions.

approach.title: Design
approach.body: We design for the whole range: flavours, sizes, languages. Mandatory text goes where it doesn't fight the main message.

approach.title: Print
approach.body: We prepare files for your printer or production line and suggest materials and finishes that fit the budget.

deliverables: A look at the shelf and the competition
Packaging or label design
Versions for the whole range: flavours, sizes, variants
Text in Uzbek, Russian and English laid out on the pack
A dieline for your pack shape
Print-ready files
Advice on materials and finishes for the budget
packaging.timeline: It depends on the number of products: a label for one product is quicker than a range of ten flavours in a box of its own shape. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins.
packaging.pricing: It depends on the number of products and the complexity: a label for one product or packaging for a whole range, a box of its own shape or a standard one. Tell us about the task and your budget, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: Can you work with our printer?
faq.a: Yes. We find out their file requirements and prepare everything to match.

faq.q: Who writes the ingredients, shelf life and other mandatory text?
faq.a: You or your technologist provide the text itself: the manufacturer is responsible for its accuracy. We lay it out carefully and make sure it's all legible.

faq.q: We already have packaging. Can you update it?
faq.a: Yes. Often a refresh is enough rather than starting over, so regular customers keep recognising you.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: The product or photos of it, the pack size and shape, the mandatory text, your printer if you've chosen one, and examples of competitors on the shelf.

ui-ux.metaTitle: UI / UX Design Services in Tashkent
ui-ux.metaDescription: Website, online shop and app design: we work out what makes it easy to use, design the screens and hand the layouts over to developers.
ui-ux.title: UI / UX Design
ui-ux.tagline: Websites and apps that are easy to use.
ui-ux.intro: A website or an app should make sense the first time: someone opens it, finds what they need, places an order. We start with who will use the product and what they need to get done. First we work out the structure and the path a user takes, then design the screens for phone and desktop, and prepare the layouts so developers can build from them easily.

approach.title: The task
approach.body: We find out who your users are, what they want to do and what gets in their way today. We look at competitors.

approach.title: Structure
approach.body: We work out which screens are needed and how people move between them, in simple sketches while changes are still easy.

approach.title: Design
approach.body: We design the screens for phone and desktop in your brand's style, with buttons and blocks that stay the same across the whole product.

approach.title: Handover
approach.body: We hand the layouts to developers in a clear form and explain how everything should work.

deliverables: Structure and user flows: how people get to their goal
Screen sketches (a prototype)
Screen designs for phone, tablet and desktop
A Figma library of buttons, fields and blocks
Notes on animations and states where they matter
Layouts ready for developers
ui-ux.timeline: It depends on scope: a landing page is quicker than an online shop or an app with user accounts. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins.
ui-ux.pricing: It depends on scope: a landing page, a website or an app, how many screens it has, and whether it needs a design system. Tell us about the task and your budget, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: We already have a website. Can you improve it instead of starting over?
faq.a: Yes. First we find where people struggle and fix that. Sometimes that's enough; sometimes starting over is the honest answer.

faq.q: Will the website be easy to use on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. We design every screen for both phone and desktop. Most people visit from their phones these days, so that's often where we start.

faq.q: Can you work with our developers?
faq.a: Yes. We hand them the layouts in a convenient form and explain how everything should work.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: Tell us what the product is, who it is for and what you expect from it. If you have a current site, analytics or user feedback, share them; it saves time.

print.metaDescription: Design for business cards, flyers, brochures, catalogues, menus, posters, books and banners. Files ready for any printer.
print.title: Print Design
print.tagline: Everything that gets printed, from a business card to a catalogue.
print.intro: We design everything that gets printed: from a business card or flyer to a catalogue, menu, book or banner. Good print rests on simple things: the text is easy to read, the main point is visible at once, and the layout prints the way it was meant to. We take the paper, the colours and the printer's requirements into account from the start, so the print run comes out the way you saw it on screen.

approach.title: The task
approach.body: We find out what needs printing, who it is for and where it will be read: at a reception desk, at a trade show, on a café table.

approach.title: Layout
approach.body: We arrange the text and images into a clear layout: the important things large, the rest in order. We show it to you and talk it through.

approach.title: Edits
approach.body: We refine it based on your comments. Before print, we check the text, phone numbers and addresses with you once more.

approach.title: Print
approach.body: We prepare files to your printer's requirements: bleed, colours, image resolution. If needed, we'll suggest paper and finishes.

deliverables: Layout design for your task
Every page typeset, for brochures, catalogues and books
Typefaces, colours and images in your brand's style
Advice on paper and finishes for the budget
Files ready for any printer
Print preparation: bleed, colour profile, image checks
print.timeline: It depends on volume: a flyer or a business card is quicker than a catalogue or a book. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins. If the print run is needed by a date — an opening, a trade show, a holiday — tell us at the start and we will plan around it.
print.pricing: It depends on format and volume: a flyer or a poster is one job, a catalogue or a book is another. Tell us what you need printed and what your budget is, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: Do you print as well?
faq.a: We design and prepare the files for printing. You can print with your own printer; we'll prepare the files to its requirements.

faq.q: We already have a brand identity. Will you stick to it?
faq.a: Yes, we'll design in your style: the same typefaces, colours and logo. If you don't have one yet, we'll choose a look that suits the task.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: What it will be (a flyer, a menu, a catalogue), the size if you know it, the text and photos, and your printer if you've chosen one. If something is missing, that's fine; we'll sort it out together.

faq.q: Do you do large formats: banners, signs, stands?
faq.a: Yes: banners, signage, trade-show stands, wayfinding in buildings. We take into account how and from what each will be made.

motion.metaDescription: Logo animation, videos for social media and ads, explainer videos, in your brand's style and in the formats you need.
motion.title: Motion Design
motion.intro: Video gets noticed faster than a still image, especially on social media. We make logo animations, short videos for social media and ads, and explainer videos about a product or service. All in your brand's style, with the same colours, typefaces and character, so it's clear at once whose video it is. We agree on the script and storyboard first and animate after: that way changes cost less.

approach.title: The task
approach.body: We find out where the video will run — social media, a screen in a venue, an ad — how long it is and what it should say.

approach.title: Script
approach.body: We write a short script and draw a storyboard showing every scene, and agree on it before animation starts.

approach.title: Animation
approach.body: We animate in 2D or 3D, whichever suits the task, and keep the movement true to the brand's character.

approach.title: Formats
approach.body: We deliver finished videos in the formats your channels need: horizontal, square, and vertical for Reels and Stories.

deliverables: Script and storyboard
Logo animation
Videos for social media and ads
Explainer videos about a product or service
Versions for different channels: 16:9, 1:1, 9:16
Animations for your website or app, if needed
motion.timeline: It depends on length and technique: a logo animation is quicker than a 3D explainer. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins. If the video is needed by a date, tell us at the start.
motion.pricing: It depends on length and technique: a logo animation, a social video or an explainer, in 2D or 3D. Tell us about the task and your budget, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: 2D or 3D: which should we choose?
faq.a: It depends on the task and the budget. 2D is quicker and suits most social videos. 3D is good when a product has to be shown from every side, but it takes longer and costs more.

faq.q: Can you make a video from our own photos and footage?
faq.a: Yes, we can add animation, titles and graphics to your footage.

faq.q: Will the video work on Instagram and Telegram?
faq.a: Yes. We'll make versions for the channels you need: vertical for Reels and Stories, square and horizontal.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: Tell us where the video will run and what it should say. Send your logo, brand identity and examples of videos you like.

strategy.metaDescription: We work out who your brand is for, what sets it apart and what it promises, so design, ads and copy all say the same thing.
strategy.title: Brand Strategy
strategy.intro: Strategy answers simple questions: who your customers are, why they should choose you over the place next door, and what you promise them. Once the answers are written down and clear to the whole team, design, advertising and copy start saying the same thing. We do strategy on its own or before branding: we talk to you and your team, study the market and competitors, and put the result into a short document you can come back to with every decision.

approach.title: Conversations
approach.body: We talk to the owners and the team, sometimes to customers: what the business does well, what it doesn't, and where you want to get to.

approach.title: The market
approach.body: We look at competitors and at how customers choose in your field, and look for a place nobody has taken yet.

approach.title: Positioning
approach.body: We put into words who the brand is for, what sets it apart and what it promises, and discuss it with leadership until everyone shares it.

approach.title: The document
approach.body: We gather it all into a clear document that designers, marketers and sales can work from.

deliverables: Findings from conversations with the team and customers
A review of the market and competitors
Portraits of your customers
Positioning: who the brand is for and what sets it apart
Key messages: what to say about yourselves, and how
A brand structure, if you have several brands
A strategy document the whole team can understand
strategy.timeline: It depends on depth: positioning for one brand takes less time than a strategy for a company with several brands. We give you the exact timing along with the price, before any work begins.
strategy.pricing: It depends on depth: positioning for one brand, or a structure for several. Tell us about the task and your budget, and we'll name a price before any work begins.

faq.q: Can we order strategy alone, without design?
faq.a: Yes. You get a document any team can work from, your own or another studio.

faq.q: How is brand strategy different from marketing strategy?
faq.a: Brand strategy answers “who are we, and why do people choose us”. Marketing strategy answers “how, where and to whom do we say it”. The first rarely changes; the second changes all the time.

faq.q: Do we really need this? We're a small business.
faq.a: A small business needs strategy just as much; it is simply simpler and shorter. Sometimes a few meetings are enough to answer the main questions and stop arguing about the logo.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: Time to talk, and a willingness to be honest about the business: what works, what doesn't and where you want to go. If you have research or customer feedback, send it over.
